record.paper_title: Computational issues for linear periodic systems: paradigms, algorithms, open problems
record.original_question: For continuous-time linear periodic systems, can one develop pole-assignment algorithms that assign desired closed-loop poles efficiently and reliably in the periodic setting?

evidence.quote: For continuous-time periodic systems, there are no algorithms for efficient computation of frequency responses, stabilisation or pole assignment.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a continuous-time linear periodic system
\[
\dot{x}(t) = A(t)\,x(t) + B(t)\,u(t), \qquad t \in \mathbb{R},
\]
where $x(t) \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $u(t) \in \mathbb{R}^m$, and the matrix-valued maps $A:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and $B:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$ are piecewise continuous and $T$-periodic, i.e. $A(t+T)=A(t)$ and $B(t+T)=B(t)$ for some fixed period $T>0$. For a $T$-periodic state-feedback gain $F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, the closed-loop system $\dot{x}(t) = (A(t)+B(t)F(t))\,x(t)$ has monodromy matrix
\[
\Phi_F(T,0) = \text{state-transition matrix from $0$ to $T$ of } A(\cdot)+B(\cdot)F(\cdot),
\]
whose eigenvalues (the characteristic multipliers of the closed-loop system) determine its Floquet/Lyapunov exponents and stability behaviour. Define the closed-loop "poles" of the periodic system as these characteristic multipliers (or, equivalently, the corresponding characteristic exponents).

Pole-assignment problem. Given a self-conjugate set $\Lambda = \{\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n\} \subset \mathbb{C}$, develop a numerical algorithm that, under suitable controllability hypotheses on $(A(\cdot),B(\cdot))$, computes a $T$-periodic feedback gain $F(\cdot)$ such that the characteristic multipliers of $A(\cdot)+B(\cdot)F(\cdot)$ coincide with $\Lambda$, and that does so:

(i) efficiently, with computational cost comparable to that of the best modern pole-assignment methods for time-invariant systems;

(ii) reliably, in a numerically stable manner that avoids explicit formation of the monodromy matrix or other ill-conditioned intermediate quantities;

(iii) directly in the continuous-time periodic setting, without recourse to lifting the system to a time-invariant or discrete-time equivalent.

Does such an algorithm exist, and if so, provide one with a complete numerical analysis (stability, conditioning, complexity, and robustness of the assignment)?
artifact.status_search_result: Numerous robust and parametric pole-assignment algorithms exist for discrete-time periodic systems and for continuous-time LTI systems via periodic (sampled-data, GSHF) feedback. However, dedicated, numerically reliable algorithms that perform pole assignment directly for continuous-time linear periodic systems with periodic state feedback—without lifting/discretization and meeting the efficiency and reliability standards of LTI counterparts—do not appear to be established in the literature surveyed. The status of the problem as posed remains unclear from available sources.

status_evidence.title: Parametric Pole Assignment and Robust Pole Assignment for Discrete-Time Linear Periodic Systems
status_evidence.snippet: A complete parametric approach for pole assignment via periodic state feedback is proposed for discrete-time periodic systems.
status_evidence.claim: Parametric pole-assignment methods exist primarily in the discrete-time periodic setting.

status_evidence.title: A robust periodic pole assignment algorithm
status_evidence.claim: Existing periodic pole-assignment algorithms target discrete-time or sampled formulations.

status_evidence.title: Pole Assignment With Improved Control Performance by Means of Periodic Feedback
status_evidence.snippet: Pole placement of continuous-time LTI systems via periodic (GSHF) feedback.
status_evidence.claim: Continuous-time treatments use periodic feedback applied to LTI systems via sampled-data lifting, not the genuine periodic-coefficient setting.
